newsitem.title: UK: Regal Hotels look to future with confidence.
newsitem.headline: Regal Hotels look to future with confidence.

text.p: Regal Hotel Group Plc said on Monday it expected to reap the benefits of its White Hart acquisition this year and expressed confidence about the future.

"With a solid foundation for the Group built, in 1997 we will get the full benefit from the White Hart acquisition and, subject to prevailing market conditions, we view the future with confidence," said executive chairman Charles Vere Nicoll.
Regal almost quadrupled its UK hotel portfolio in 1996 when it acquired 60 White Hart properties from Granada for 122 million pounds. Regal now has 82 hotels in the provincial three-star sector.
The company's 1996 pre-tax profit soared to 10.4 million pounds from 2.9 million in 1995. Earnings per share increased by 38 percent to 4.68p from 3.39p.
"We are ahead of where people expected us to be," Vere Nicolll told Reuters.
Occupancy and room rates at the White Hart hotels were flat in 1996 but Vere Nicoll said that profitability at the new hotels had improved "by seven percentage points".
"We intend to take that solid base and grow it in year two," he added.
Regal Hotels is hoping to develop a partnership announced last year with the Carlson Group of Companies to exploit their Country Inn & Suites brand in the UK.
Regal plans to convert a hotel in the western English town of Swindon to the brand. Under the deal, Carlson gets two percent of room revenue.

Vere Nicoll noted that the agreement gave Regal Hotels a link to Carlson Wagonlits Travel, one of the world's leading travel agencies. Carlson also operates brand names such as TGI Friday's restaurants and Radisson hotels.
